name: Hiel
overview: Hiel was a male figure known as the Bethelite who undertook the rebuilding of Jericho. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his notable action is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34. There are no additional personal notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hiel means 'G-d [El] lives here,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This proper name is noted in 1 Kings 16:34 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Hiel was the father of Abiram and Segub, as mentioned in 1 Kings 16:34. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Hiel's significance lies in his role in rebuilding the city of Jericho, an event noted in 1 Kings 16:34. This act is historically and spiritually important because Jericho was a city famously destroyed under God's command during the conquest of Canaan. His rebuilding effort marks a notable moment in Israel's history, demonstrating human initiative in a city with a profound biblical legacy.
